title: The normalized edge is invertible in the lowest cohomology degree
statement: In [def-pur-conventions], let $Y$ be a scheme, $q\in\mathbf Z$, and $e:H^qR\Gamma(Y,-)\to\Gamma(Y,H^q(-))$ a natural map satisfying the explicit cocycle normalization `EdgeNormalization` of [lem-pur-retracted-support-localization-comparison]. For every derived pro-etale module sheaf $K$ with $H^i(K)=0$ for $i<q$, $e_K$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: second paragraph, canonical edge comparison, with first-paragraph good truncation

proof.text: Good truncation followed by a bounded-below injective resolution gives a K-injective representative I of K that is zero below q. Both I and its global-section complex have no degree-q boundaries, so their cycles-to-homology projections are invertible.

Global sections preserve the kernel of the degree-q differential. The normalization equation therefore identifies the composite of the invertible global cycles-to-homology map and e with a composite of kernel-comparison and homology-factorization isomorphisms. Cancel the invertible first factor. Naturality along the representative isomorphism gives invertibility at K.

proof_origin.place: second paragraph, canonical edge comparison, with first-paragraph good truncation
